Suggested commercial / deal terms for Exec approval: 

1) Reservation hold: place a temporary H100 reservation hold for 2 weeks (05 Oct — 19 Oct). No upfront commitment fee; customer billed only for consumed hours. Redwood to guarantee preemption-free burst capacity up to 500 GPU-hours across the window.

2) Pilot concession: 15% credit applied to the billed consumption during the pilot period (one-time credit on first invoice).

3) Overage cap: Overages beyond the 500 GPU-hour buffer billed at a capped rate of $12.50 / GPU-hour (not to exceed this cap) for the pilot window.

4) Fallback policy: In case H100 capacity is constrained, Redwood will automatically route to L4i-compatible instances with a performance notice; MedAI can elect to pause burst.

5) Legal / Billing steps: need a 1-page addendum signed (DocuSign) to confirm the temporary reservation hold and overage cap. I attached a short term-sheet (MedAI_pilot-term-sheet.pdf) for signature.

Rationale: 15% pilot credit + capped overage protects MedAI budget while avoiding material long-term concession. The capped overage ($12.50/hr) keeps unit economics defined for our finance team.

Next step: Markus — can you escalate to Grace for final approval? If Grace signs off we can send the DocuSign addendum to procurement today.

Best,

- Recommendation: include a clause that allows temporary fallback to performance-equivalent instances (H100 or highest-available L4 family) with prior notice.

I’ve attached a short compatibility note (H100_compatibility-note.txt) showing expected perf deltas and recommended pre-warm steps.
